message.text:
I need to identify which background runners the server actually starts and what triggers their scheduling. I will also check for any unused scheduling infrastructure.

I found s3presign and memopayload runners under server/runner/, plus a backgroundRunner reference in server.go. I am now exploring these further.

args.command:
ls /bench/repo/server/runner; echo '===='; grep -n -i "runner\|ticker\|cron\|schedule\|Start\|background\|go func" /bench/repo/server/server.go /bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go
echo '==== runner files ===='
find /bench/repo/server/runner /bench/repo/internal -iname '*schedul*' -o -iname '*runner*' -o -iname '*cron*' -o -iname '*ticker*' 2>/dev/null
echo '==== startBackground ===='
grep -rn "Start\|Run\|ticker\|time.NewTicker\|cron" --include='*.go' /bench/repo/server/runner /bench/repo/server/server.go

message.text:
The server starts the s3presign runner. It runs once immediately on startup. Then it runs every 12 hours via a ticker. This is wired in server/server.go. No other background runners are started.

The memopayload runner is not started by the server. The internal/scheduler cron package exists but is unused. Webhook workers, SSE heartbeats, and cache cleanup tickers are not server-started runners.

message.text: The server only starts s3presign. memopayload.NewRunner and scheduler.New are never invoked by the server itself; both appear only in tests and documentation. No scheduling infrastructure used by the server is unused.

q28.
s3presign — immediate RunOnce on startup, then every 12 hours via time.Ticker (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`, started from `server/server.go`)
unused: `internal/scheduler` (cron job scheduler) is never started by the server; `server/runner/memopayload` is only used as `RebuildMemoPayload` on create/update, not as a background runner

`startBackgroundRunners` in `server/server.go` constructs `s3presign.NewRunner`, calls `RunOnce`, then `Run` in a goroutine. No other runner is launched there.
